identity.question: Will Trump be impeached by December 31, 2026?

frozen_rule: House simple-majority vote to approve/pass one or more articles of impeachment of President Donald Trump between 2025-07-24 and 2026-12-31 11:59 PM ET qualifies YES. Senate trial, conviction, or removal unnecessary. US federal-government information primary; credible-reporting consensus fallback.

facts.claim: Official Clerk homepage snapshot labels House at a Glance as of October 19, 2026: Republicans 218, Democrats 214, Independents 1, vacancies 2 (435 seats total).
facts.limitations: Snapshot dated Oct 19, not an independently refreshed seat-by-seat roster; captured Members page repeats totals but its rendered vacancy-detail section did not expose names.

facts.claim: Clerk Roll Call 322, Dec 11, 2025, H.Res.939, “Impeaching Donald John Trump…”: question was “On Motion to Table”; motion passed 237 yea, 140 nay, 47 present, 9 not voting. A successful motion to table is a procedural disposition, not House approval/passage of articles under this market rule.
facts.limitations: This exact vote record establishes that vote only; no comprehensive roll-call, bill-status, committee or proceedings sweep was performed for the full July 24, 2025–Dec 31, 2026 window.

facts.claim: House.gov Legislative Activity page retrieved Oct 20 says “There is no legislative activity available at this time”; it renders 2026 monthly calendars through November, including future November dates marked as in-session and district-work days. December 2026 calendar was not present in this captured page.
facts.limitations: The page describes a calendar as an agenda of possible business; no specific impeachment vote was listed. It does not prove December floor plans or absence of a pending vote.

source_gaps: No broad claim that no articles passed in the entire operative window: only one identified impeachment-related roll-call result was captured, and it was a motion to table.
No verified current December 2026 House floor calendar or relevant scheduled/pending impeachment vote in the bounded four-request set.
Formal introduction or committee/procedural action is not equivalent to House passage of articles; further government-record coverage would be required to support any full-window absence claim.
limits: Factual collection only. No probability, forecast, verdict, ranking, ledger entry, or action.
